Five days after I graduated high school, I got hired at a fairly nice drug store (local, only two locations). After two days or so, I was finally left to myself to work the cash register. I was so excited to be making money! Then my world came crashing down.

A middle aged man half carrying a rather large woman came in through the automatic doors. When she came close enough, she flung herself from the man's steady arms and onto my counter.

Her: Benadryl!

I was completely confounded. I just looked at her with what I'm sure was a stupid look on my face.

Her: Damn it! GIVE ME BENADRYL!

Me: Uh, it's in aisle 9 I believe.

Her: No, I need it NOW!

Me: I'm sorry... I don't have any up here.

Her: I'm having a reaction! I'm going into anaphylactic shock. I'm going to die!

The guy, who I assume was her husband, explained that she was stung by a bee outside.

Now, before this point, I had never heard of anaphylactic shock. I did know that some people are crazy allergic to bee stings, though, so I quickly called the pharmacy at the back of the store. I must have been pretty panicked because one of the pharmacy techs came running with a cup of pills. The woman quickly gobbled them down (she was still basically lying on my counter), and then within ten second stood back up as if nothing was wrong with her.

Her: I could have died . You know that, right? And it would have been your fault.

She waddled back to her husband and took his arm. They both went outside. The pharmacy tech gave me a quizzical look, then returned to the pharmacy.

A couple minutes later, the manager came up to me and asked me to explain everything that had happened. He said that it was grounds for termination, but since I didn't know any better, he'd let me off the hook.

Me: What exactly did I do wrong?

Manager: You can't just give people medicine. It's an insurance issue. If you had given her medicine and she would have died, her family could have owned this store.

Me: Well... I didn't. (Pharmacy tech) did.

Manager: Your first instinct should have been to call me.

Me: She told me she was dying! What would you have done?!

Manager: She was an insurance liability. I would have asked her to leave the store and called 911.

So not only did I have what I believed to be a hypochondriac scare the crap out of me, but my manager told me that I could have been fired for the whole ordeal.

This wasn't even the craziest thing that happened during my three months there.
Holy Crap! Well, makes for a good story anyway. :D
Wow. Some people (the manager) are just incredible. Were you shaking the rest of the day ?

If that lady was seriously about to die from said bee sting, oral diphenhydramine would not have been the solution... She would have needed an epi-pen and a trip to the ER...

And the manager... "I would have asked her to leave the store", what the hell.
